Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be bounded and
open, and let $H,V$ be the closure spaces defined above. There is a constant $C$ independent of $\Omega$
and $a$ such that every $a\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ satisfies
$$\|a\|_{L^6(\Omega)}\le C\|\nabla a\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad \|a\|_{L^4(\Omega)}\le\|a\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^{1/4}\|a\|_{L^6(\Omega)}^{3/4}.$$
For $T>0$, if $u\in L^\infty(0,T;H)\cap L^2(0,T;V)$, then
$u\in L^{8/3}(0,T;L^4(\Omega))$. Here the time-dependent $L^p$ notation
means strong measurability and integrability of the displayed norm; the
continuous embedding $V\to L^4(\Omega)$ carries strongly measurable
$V$-valued maps to strongly measurable $L^4$-valued maps. Let $V^*$ be the
continuous real-linear dual of $V$ with its operator norm. Choose any strongly measurable representative $\widetilde u:(0,T)\to V$ of the $L^2(0,T;V)$ class of $u$; through the embedding $V\to H$, it represents the same $H$-valued class almost everywhere. For almost every $t\in(0,T)$ define
$$b_u(t)(\phi)=-\int_\Omega \widetilde u_i(t,x)\widetilde u_j(t,x)\partial_j\phi_i(x)dx,\qquad\phi\in V,$$
and assign $b_u(t)=0$ on any exceptional null set. Then $b_u(t)\in V^*$ for almost every $t$, $t\mapsto b_u(t)$ is strongly measurable, and its equivalence class is independent of the chosen representative $\widetilde u$. This class belongs to $L^{4/3}(0,T;V^*)$ and satisfies
$$\|b_u(t)\|_{V^*}\le\|\widetilde u(t)\|_{L^4(\Omega)}^2\quad\text{for almost every }t\in(0,T).$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, $L>0$, $\nu>0$, and $u_0\in H$ for the
periodic solenoidal Fourier spaces on $\mathbb T_L^d$. Let $u$ be any global
unforced periodic Leray–Hopf solution with data $(\nu,u_0)$ supplied by Global
periodic weak viscous existence under these hypotheses. Put
$U=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb T_L^d$, and let $\mathcal D_{\rm per}(U)$ be the
space of smooth complex-valued functions on $U$, represented by smooth
$L$-periodic lifts in space, that are compactly supported in time. For tests
supported in a fixed compact interval $K\subset(0,\infty)$, use the seminorms
$$p_{K,m}(\phi)=\max_{j+|\alpha|\le m}\sup_{(t,x)\in K\times\mathbb T_L^d}|\partial_t^j\partial_x^\alpha\phi(t,x)|\qquad(m\in\mathbb N_0);$$
equip $\mathcal D_{\rm per}(U)$ with the locally convex inductive-limit
topology over these fixed-time-support spaces, generated by all seminorms whose
restriction to every fixed-time-support space is continuous. A spacetime distribution means a
continuous complex-linear functional on this test space; all pairings are
bilinear, and derivatives act by transposing the corresponding test derivative
with a minus sign. Then there is a unique mean-zero-in-space
distribution $\pi$ on $(0,\infty)\times\mathbb T_L^d$ such that
$\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)+\nabla\pi=\nu\Delta u$
as a spacetime distribution, normalized by requiring its zero spatial Fourier
coefficient to vanish. Specifically, for $k\in\mathbb Z^d$, its $k$th spatial
Fourier coefficient is the time distribution defined by
$\langle\widehat\pi(k),\psi\rangle=\langle\pi,\psi(t)e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x}\rangle$
for $\psi\in C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\mathbb C)$, with the spacetime
distribution pairing taken using $dt\,L^{-d}dx$ and extended complex-linearly;
normalization means $\widehat\pi(0)=0$. No
function-space or pointwise regularity for $\pi$ is
asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $a_i<b_i$ for $i=1,2,3$ and let
$\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3(a_i,b_i)\subset\mathbb R^3$ be the resulting finite open
rectangle, let $\nu>0$ and $u_0\in H$ for the bounded closure spaces on this
page, and let $u$ be a global weak velocity supplied for these data by the
bounded no-slip weak existence theorem on this page. Assume the rectangular divergence-inverse
result: there is a continuous linear map
$R:D_0(\Omega)\to C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, where
$D_0(\Omega)=\{h\in C_c^\infty(\Omega):\int_\Omega h=0\}$, such that
$\operatorname{div}Rh=h$. For each compact $K\subset\Omega$ there is a compact
$K'\subset\Omega$ containing the support of $Rh$ whenever $h$ is supported in
$K$, and on each fixed-support test space $R$ is continuous for all seminorms
$\sup|\partial^\alpha h|$. Then there is a spacetime distribution $\pi$ with
$$\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)+\nabla\pi=\nu\Delta u$$
on $(0,\infty)\times\Omega$. Its normalization may be fixed by any
$\theta\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $\int_\Omega\theta=1$ through
$\langle\pi,a(t)\theta(x)\rangle=0$ for every compactly supported smooth
temporal test $a$. Pressure is unique under this normalization. This is a
conditional distributional statement and gives no $L^2$ pressure estimate,
corner regularity, or pointwise boundary traction. Here
$(u\otimes u):\nabla\psi=\sum_{i,j}u_i u_j\partial_j\psi_i$.

open, and let $H,V$ be the closure spaces defined above. There is a constant $C$ independent of $\Omega$
and $a$ such that every $a\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ satisfies
$$\|a\|_{L^6(\Omega)}\le C\|\nabla a\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad \|a\|_{L^4(\Omega)}\le\|a\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^{1/4}\|a\|_{L^6(\Omega)}^{3/4}.$$
For $T>0$, if $u\in L^\infty(0,T;H)\cap L^2(0,T;V)$, then
$u\in L^{8/3}(0,T;L^4(\Omega))$. Here the time-dependent $L^p$ notation
means strong measurability and integrability of the displayed norm; the
continuous embedding $V\to L^4(\Omega)$ carries strongly measurable
$V$-valued maps to strongly measurable $L^4$-valued maps. Let $V^*$ be the
continuous real-linear dual of $V$ with its operator norm. Choose any strongly measurable representative $\widetilde u:(0,T)\to V$ of the $L^2(0,T;V)$ class of $u$; through the embedding $V\to H$, it represents the same $H$-valued class almost everywhere. For almost every $t\in(0,T)$ define
$$b_u(t)(\phi)=-\int_\Omega \widetilde u_i(t,x)\widetilde u_j(t,x)\partial_j\phi_i(x)dx,\qquad\phi\in V,$$
and assign $b_u(t)=0$ on any exceptional null set. Then $b_u(t)\in V^*$ for almost every $t$, $t\mapsto b_u(t)$ is strongly measurable, and its equivalence class is independent of the chosen representative $\widetilde u$. This class belongs to $L^{4/3}(0,T;V^*)$ and satisfies
$$\|b_u(t)\|_{V^*}\le\|\widetilde u(t)\|_{L^4(\Omega)}^2\quad\text{for almost every }t\in(0,T).$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, $L>0$, $\nu>0$, and $u_0\in H$ for the
periodic solenoidal Fourier spaces on $\mathbb T_L^d$. Let $u$ be any global
unforced periodic Leray–Hopf solution with data $(\nu,u_0)$ supplied by Global
periodic weak viscous existence under these hypotheses. Put
$U=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb T_L^d$, and let $\mathcal D_{\rm per}(U)$ be the
space of smooth complex-valued functions on $U$, represented by smooth
$L$-periodic lifts in space, that are compactly supported in time. For tests
supported in a fixed compact interval $K\subset(0,\infty)$, use the seminorms
$$p_{K,m}(\phi)=\max_{j+|\alpha|\le m}\sup_{(t,x)\in K\times\mathbb T_L^d}|\partial_t^j\partial_x^\alpha\phi(t,x)|\qquad(m\in\mathbb N_0);$$
equip $\mathcal D_{\rm per}(U)$ with the locally convex inductive-limit
topology over these fixed-time-support spaces, generated by all seminorms whose
restriction to every fixed-time-support space is continuous. A spacetime distribution means a
continuous complex-linear functional on this test space; all pairings are
bilinear, and derivatives act by transposing the corresponding test derivative
with a minus sign. Then there is a unique mean-zero-in-space
distribution $\pi$ on $(0,\infty)\times\mathbb T_L^d$ such that
$\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)+\nabla\pi=\nu\Delta u$
as a spacetime distribution, normalized by requiring its zero spatial Fourier
coefficient to vanish. Specifically, for $k\in\mathbb Z^d$, its $k$th spatial
Fourier coefficient is the time distribution defined by
$\langle\widehat\pi(k),\psi\rangle=\langle\pi,\psi(t)e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x}\rangle$
for $\psi\in C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\mathbb C)$, with the spacetime
distribution pairing taken using $dt\,L^{-d}dx$ and extended complex-linearly;
normalization means $\widehat\pi(0)=0$. No
function-space or pointwise regularity for $\pi$ is
asserted.

page, and let $u$ be a global weak velocity supplied for these data by the
bounded no-slip weak existence theorem on this page. Assume the rectangular divergence-inverse
result: there is a continuous linear map
$R:D_0(\Omega)\to C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, where
$D_0(\Omega)=\{h\in C_c^\infty(\Omega):\int_\Omega h=0\}$, such that
$\operatorname{div}Rh=h$. For each compact $K\subset\Omega$ there is a compact
$K'\subset\Omega$ containing the support of $Rh$ whenever $h$ is supported in
$K$, and on each fixed-support test space $R$ is continuous for all seminorms
$\sup|\partial^\alpha h|$. Then there is a spacetime distribution $\pi$ with
$$\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)+\nabla\pi=\nu\Delta u$$
on $(0,\infty)\times\Omega$. Its normalization may be fixed by any
$\theta\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $\int_\Omega\theta=1$ through
$\langle\pi,a(t)\theta(x)\rangle=0$ for every compactly supported smooth
temporal test $a$. Pressure is unique under this normalization. This is a
conditional distributional statement and gives no $L^2$ pressure estimate,
corner regularity, or pointwise boundary traction. Here

before.quote:
A bounded wall domain is a bounded connected open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ with $C^2$ boundary. Its classical velocity class on $[0,T]$ is $C^1([0,T];C^2(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^3))$; a pressure in this class is continuous in time with one continuous spatial derivative. The boundary normal $n$ is the outward unit normal. A no-slip trace is $u|_{\partial\Omega}=0$, a prescribed moving-wall trace is $u|_{\partial\Omega}=g$, and an impermeable trace is $u\cdot n=0$; these are distinct boundary data.

An exterior domain is $\Omega_{\mathrm{ext}}=\mathbb R^3\setminus K$, where $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ is compact with $C^2$ boundary and $\Omega_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is connected. The exterior classical velocity and pressure classes have the same local regularity up to $\partial K$ on every compact spatial subset. The domain definition alone imposes no condition at infinity. An exterior energy argument must state additional decay or weighted-space hypotheses. We call the explicit bounds $|u(t,x)|=O(|x|^{-2})$, $|\nabla u(t,x)|=O(|x|^{-3})$, and $|p(t,x)|=O(|x|^{-2})$, uniform for $t\in[0,T]$, a cutoff-decay condition; this is additional solution data, not part of the bare exterior domain, and no energy identity follows from this definition alone.

A bounded wall domain is a bounded connected open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ with $C^2$ boundary. For $T>0$, its classical velocity fields are maps $u:[0,T]\times\overline\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ in $C^1([0,T];C^2(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^3))$, and its classical pressures are maps $p:[0,T]\times\overline\Omega\to\mathbb R$ in $C([0,T];C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R))$. Here spatial derivatives through the indicated order extend continuously to the boundary, and time continuity and differentiability are taken in the corresponding spatial supremum norms. The boundary normal $n$ is the outward unit normal. A no-slip trace is $u|_{\partial\Omega}=0$, a prescribed moving-wall trace is $u|_{\partial\Omega}=g$, and an impermeable trace is $u\cdot n=0$; these are distinct boundary data.

An exterior domain is $\Omega_{\mathrm{ext}}=\mathbb R^3\setminus K$, where $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ is compact with $C^2$ boundary and $\Omega_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is connected. The exterior classical fields are maps $u:[0,T]\times\overline\Omega_{\mathrm{ext}}\to\mathbb R^3$ and $p:[0,T]\times\overline\Omega_{\mathrm{ext}}\to\mathbb R$, with $u\in C^1([0,T];C^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\overline\Omega_{\mathrm{ext}};\mathbb R^3))$ and $p\in C([0,T];C^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\overline\Omega_{\mathrm{ext}};\mathbb R))$. The local spaces require the indicated spatial derivatives to extend continuously up to $\partial K$; their topology is uniform convergence of those derivatives on each compact subset of the closure. The domain definition alone imposes no condition at infinity. An exterior energy argument must state additional decay or weighted-space hypotheses. We call the explicit bounds $|u(t,x)|=O(|x|^{-2})$, $|\nabla u(t,x)|=O(|x|^{-3})$, and $|p(t,x)|=O(|x|^{-2})$, uniform for $t\in[0,T]$, a cutoff-decay condition; this is additional solution data, not part of the bare exterior domain, and no energy identity follows from this definition alone.

Let $d\ge2$ be an integer, and let $L>0$ be the numerical period in a fixed
length unit. Let
$\mathbb T_L^d=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^d$ carry normalized Lebesgue measure
$L^{-d}dx$. For $k\in\mathbb Z^d$ put
$\kappa_k=2\pi k/L$ and $e_k(x)=\exp(i\kappa_k\cdot x)$. For a complex
scalar or vector $L^2$ class $f$, let
$\widehat f(k)=L^{-d}\int_{[0,L]^d}f(x)e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x}\,dx$;
real fields are the classes satisfying
$\widehat f(-k)=\overline{\widehat f(k)}$. For $s\ge0$, let
$$H^s(\mathbb T_L^d)=\left\{f\in L^2:\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}(1+L^2|\kappa_k|^2)^s|\widehat f(k)|^2<\infty\right\},$$
with norm given by the square root of this sum; the weight is dimensionless.
Under Countable Choice the coefficient map is injective, so this is a norm.
The real solenoidal spaces are
$$H=\{u\in L^2(\mathbb T_L^d;\mathbb R^d): k\cdot\widehat u(k)=0\text{ for every }k\ne0\},\qquad V=H\cap H^1(\mathbb T_L^d;\mathbb R^d).$$
The zero Fourier mode is unrestricted. Under Countable Choice, the supplied
Fourier-basis theorem makes the coefficient map a surjective isometry from
$L^2$ onto $\ell^2$; the coefficient-space norm identifications and the
equivalence between Fourier divergence and distributional divergence in this
definition use that hypothesis. Under the same assumption, the orthogonal
solenoidal projection $P$ is well-defined on $L^2$ and has multiplier
$P_0=I$ and
$P_k=I-\kappa_k\kappa_k^{\mathsf T}/|\kappa_k|^2$ for $k\ne0$. For integer
$N\ge0$, rectangular truncation $\Pi_N$ keeps precisely $|k|_\infty\le N$. A weak
derivative in coordinate $j$ has Fourier coefficient $i\kappa_{k,j}\widehat f(k)$.
For $r>0$, $H^{-r}$ is the Hilbert completion of finite complex Fourier
coefficient sequences in the norm squared
$\sum_k(1+L^2|\kappa_k|^2)^{-r}|\widehat f(k)|^2$; its real subspace is the
completion of the conjugate-symmetric sequences.

$\widehat f(-k)=\overline{\widehat f(k)}$.

$$p_m(\varphi)=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\sup_{x\in\mathbb T_L^d}|\partial^\alpha\varphi(x)|\qquad(m\in\mathbb N_0).$$
A periodic distribution is a continuous complex-linear functional on this test space, with bilinear pairing. Its derivative is defined by
$$\langle\partial_j T,\varphi\rangle=-\langle T,\partial_j\varphi\rangle.$$

$$\langle\operatorname{div}U,\varphi\rangle=-\sum_{j=1}^d\langle U_j,\partial_j\varphi\rangle.$$

$$\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}u(x)\cdot\nabla\varphi(x)\,L^{-d}dx=0\qquad(\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb T_L^d;\mathbb C)).$$

definition use that hypothesis. Under the same assumption, the orthogonal

derivative in coordinate $j$ has Fourier coefficient $i\kappa_{k,j}\widehat f(k)$.
For $r>0$, $H^{-r}$ is the Hilbert completion of finite complex Fourier

For the fixed-support spaces of [[def-fixed-support-test-function-frechet-space]], let $\mathcal P$ be the set of all seminorms $q:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to[0,\infty)$ such that $q|_{\mathcal D_K}$ is continuous for every compact $K\subseteq\Omega$. A seminorm means $q(av)=|a|q(v)$ and $q(v+w)\le q(v)+q(w)$.

The **test-function topology** is the topology generated by translated finite intersections of sets $\{\varphi:q(\varphi)<\varepsilon\}$, where $q\in\mathcal P$ and $\varepsilon>0$. Equivalently it is the finest locally convex topology making every inclusion $\mathcal D_K\to\mathcal D(\Omega)$ continuous; the universal-property lemma below proves this equivalence and the topology assertions.

after.quote:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open. For the fixed-support spaces of [[def-fixed-support-test-function-frechet-space]], let $\mathcal P$ be the set of all seminorms $q:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to[0,\infty)$ such that $q|_{\mathcal D_K}$ is continuous for every compact $K\subseteq\Omega$. A seminorm means $q(av)=|a|q(v)$ and $q(v+w)\le q(v)+q(w)$.

The **test-function topology** is the topology generated by translated finite intersections of sets $\{\varphi:q(\varphi)<\varepsilon\}$, where $q\in\mathcal P$ and $\varepsilon>0$. Equivalently it is the finest locally convex topology making every inclusion $\mathcal D_K\hookrightarrow\mathcal D(\Omega)$ continuous; the universal-property lemma below proves this equivalence and the topology assertions. This is the locally convex inductive-limit or **LF topology**, not the unrestricted final topology of arbitrary spaces.

For precision, a locally convex topology here is a vector topology generated by a family of seminorms, and boundedness means absorption by every zero-neighborhood: for each such neighborhood $U$ there is $t>0$ with $B\subseteq tU$. Finite intersections may be empty, giving the whole space. When $\Omega$ is empty there is only the zero vector and its unique topology. No convergence criterion for sequences is used in the definition; that criterion will be a theorem.

**General random-state interface.** Let $X$ be a specified separable real Banach space with its norm-Borel sigma-algebra, let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space, and let $U:\Omega\to X$ be strongly measurable: measurable finite-valued simple maps converge to $U$ in norm outside a measurable null set. A finite-second-moment state satisfies $\mathbb E\|U\|_X^2<\infty$. Finite collections of bounded linear maps $L_j:X\to\mathbb R$ are bounded sensors; their operator bounds are $|L_j(x)|\le C_j\|x\|_X$ with supplied finite $C_j$. When used as a physical model, specify whether randomness describes initial data, forcing, measurement, or an adopted stochastic closure. None of those interpretations follows from deterministic balance equations. This interface asserts no PDE or existence of a measurable solution selection.

**Spatial velocity law and integral sensor.** Let $d\ge1$ be an integer and let $(D,\mathcal D,\lambda)$ be a finite measure space with $0<\lambda(D)<\infty$, interpreted as a spatial region with volume measure $\lambda$. Let $H:=L^2(D,\lambda;\mathbb R^d)$ consist of almost-everywhere equivalence classes of measurable vector fields $v$ with $\int_D|v(x)|^2\,d\lambda(x)<\infty$, where $|\cdot|$ is the Euclidean norm. Give $H$ the norm $\|v\|_H:=(\int_D|v(x)|^2\,d\lambda(x))^{1/2}$ and its norm topology; this is the finite direct sum of the scalar $L^2$ norms. Write $\mathcal B(H)$ for the sigma-algebra generated by the norm-open subsets of $H$. A finite-second-moment random velocity law is a probability measure $\mu$ on $(H,\mathcal B(H))$ such that
$$\int_H \|v\|_H^2\,d\mu(v)<\infty.$$
For a sensor weight $\psi\in H$, define the ideal linear sensor and its centered observable by
$$S_\psi(v):=\int_D v(x)\cdot\psi(x)\,d\lambda(x),\qquad f_\psi(v):=S_\psi(v)-\int_H S_\psi(w)\,d\mu(w).$$
The sensor reads a weighted spatial average; it does not represent a point evaluation. When $v$ is assigned SI velocity units of metres per second and $\lambda$ is volume in $\mathrm m^d$, assigning $\psi$ units $\mathrm m^{-d}$ makes $S_\psi(v)$ a velocity. Other weight units multiply the sensor units by the corresponding factor. The centered observable is dimensionally the same as the sensor reading.

Let $I$ be an open time interval in seconds and let $\Omega=\prod_{j=1}^3(\mathbb R/L_j\mathbb Z)$, with fixed periods $L_j>0$ in metres. Give $\Omega$ the completed, unnormalised pushforward of Lebesgue measure on $C=\prod_{j=1}^3[0,L_j)$ under the quotient map, as in the kinetic-density definition. Let $f:\Omega\times\mathbb R^3\times I\to(0,\infty)$ be $C^1$ in $(x,t)$ and $C^2$ in $v$, with $v$ measured in metres per second and $f$ in the units assigned by the kinetic-density definition. Fix a constant $f_{\rm ref}>0$ with the same units as $f$. Put $\ell=\log(f/f_{\rm ref})$, $A=f(x,v,t)f(x,w,t)$, and $B=f(x,v',t)f(x,w',t)$. Use the elastic collision set $Q_{\rm el}=\{(v,w,v',w')\in\mathbb R^{12}:v+w=v'+w',\ |v|^2+|w|^2=|v'|^2+|w'|^2\}$ with its relative Borel sigma-algebra and the nonnegative countably additive measure $\nu$ invariant under particle exchange in either pair and incoming/outgoing interchange, together with the weak operator $Q_\nu$ from the elastic-collision definition. Assume for each $t$ that $f$, $f|v|^2$, and $f|\ell|$ are integrable over $\Omega\times\mathbb R^3$. On each compact time interval assume a common integrable envelope in $(x,v)$ for $|(1+\ell)\partial_t f|$; at each $t$ assume $(1+|\ell|)|v\cdot\nabla_x f|$ is integrable over $\Omega\times\mathbb R^3$. In addition, assume
$$f(1+|v|)|\ell|,\quad (1+|\ell|)|\partial_t f|,\quad (1+|\ell|)|v|\,|\nabla_x f|\in L^1_{\rm loc}(I\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^3,dt\,dx\,dv),$$
so the entropy density, entropy flux, and local differentiation terms are integrable on compact time-space regions. Define
$$D(x,t):=\frac14\int_{Q_{\rm el}}(A-B)\log(A/B)\,d\nu.$$
Assume that $D$ is measurable and locally integrable on $I\times\Omega$, and that for each $t$ its spatial section belongs to $L^1(\Omega)$. At every $(x,t)$ assume $f(x,\cdot,t)\in\mathcal D_\nu$ and $1,\ell(x,\cdot,t)\in\mathcal S_{f(x,\cdot,t)}$, with the measurability and absolute-convergence conditions of the elastic-collision definition. With $\delta\varphi=\varphi(v)+\varphi(w)-\varphi(v')-\varphi(w')$, assume
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\varphi(v)Q_\nu(f)(v)\,dv=\frac14\int_{Q_{\rm el}}(B-A)\delta\varphi\,d\nu$$
for those two tests, and suppose $\partial_t f+v\cdot\nabla_x f=Q_\nu(f)$. Define
$$h(x,t):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f\log(f/f_{\rm ref})\,dv,\qquad J_H(x,t):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}v f\log(f/f_{\rm ref})\,dv,$$
$$H(t):=\int_\Omega h(x,t)\,dx,\qquad D_{\rm tot}(t):=\int_\Omega D(x,t)\,dx.$$
Then the local entropy balance holds in distributions: for every $\eta\in C_c^\infty(I\times\Omega)$,
$$\int_I\int_\Omega\bigl(h\,\partial_t\eta+J_H\cdot\nabla_x\eta-D\eta\bigr)\,dx\,dt=0.$$
Moreover, $D(x,t)\ge0$ for almost every $(x,t)$. The periodic global entropy $H$ is differentiable and
$$\frac{dH}{dt}=-D_{\rm tot}(t)\le0.$$
The inequality is conditional on the adopted weak collision identity; it is not a derivation from reversible many-particle mechanics or a kinetic-PDE existence theorem.

Fix the particle mass $m>0$ in kilograms, Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin, and velocity Lebesgue measure $dv$ from the kinetic-density definition. Put $v_*=1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $\omega_3(v)=\sum_{j=0}^3(|v|/v_*)^j$. Here $v\in\mathbb R^3$ is measured in metres per second, and $f$ is a number density in velocity space with units $\mathrm{s^3\,m^{-6}}$. For a finite-valued nonnegative measurable velocity density $f:\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ with finite absolute third moment $\int\omega_3(v)f(v)\,dv<\infty$, set $n:=\int f\,dv$. Where $n>0$, set $u:=n^{-1}\int vf\,dv$ and $T:=m(3k_Bn)^{-1}\int|v-u|^2f\,dv$; then $n$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, $u$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and $T$ has units kelvins. Define the admissible BGK input domain
$$\mathcal D_{\rm BGK}:=\left\{f:\int\omega_3f\,dv<\infty,\ f\ge0\text{ finite-valued measurable},\ n>0,\ \int|v-u|^2f\,dv>0\right\}.$$
For $f\in\mathcal D_{\rm BGK}$, the temperature $T$ is strictly positive, $\theta:=k_BT/m$ has units $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-2}}$, and the moment-matched Maxwellian $M[f]$ and relaxation operator are defined by the following formulas; $M[f]$ has the same units as $f$:
$$M[f](v):=n(2\pi\theta)^{-3/2}\exp(-|v-u|^2/(2\theta)),\qquad Q_{\rm BGK}(f):=\frac{M[f]-f}{\tau}.$$
For fixed relaxation time $\tau>0$ measured in seconds, the displayed formula defines the single-species Bhatnagar–Gross–Krook (BGK) relaxation operator pointwise on $\mathcal D_{\rm BGK}$, with $Q_{\rm BGK}(f)$ in units of $f$ per second. The corresponding accelerated homogeneous model with dimensionless parameter $\epsilon>0$ is $\partial_t f=Q_{\rm BGK}(f)/\epsilon$. Outside $\mathcal D_{\rm BGK}$ this item assigns no BGK operator. This is a prescribed relaxation model. It is distinct from the binary collision operator and does not by itself assert a derivation from microscopic mechanics or an inhomogeneous hydrodynamic limit.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be bounded and
open, and let $H,V$ be the closure spaces defined above. There is a constant $C$ independent of $\Omega$
and $a$ such that every $a\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ satisfies
$$\|a\|_{L^6(\Omega)}\le C\|\nabla a\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad \|a\|_{L^4(\Omega)}\le\|a\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^{1/4}\|a\|_{L^6(\Omega)}^{3/4}.$$
For $T>0$, if $u\in L^\infty(0,T;H)\cap L^2(0,T;V)$, then
$u\in L^{8/3}(0,T;L^4(\Omega))$. Here the time-dependent $L^p$ notation
means strong measurability and integrability of the displayed norm; the
continuous embedding $V\to L^4(\Omega)$ carries strongly measurable
$V$-valued maps to strongly measurable $L^4$-valued maps. Let $V^*$ be the
continuous real-linear dual of $V$ with its operator norm. Choose any strongly measurable representative $\widetilde u:(0,T)\to V$ of the $L^2(0,T;V)$ class of $u$; through the embedding $V\to H$, it represents the same $H$-valued class almost everywhere. For almost every $t\in(0,T)$ define
$$b_u(t)(\phi)=-\int_\Omega \widetilde u_i(t,x)\widetilde u_j(t,x)\partial_j\phi_i(x)dx,\qquad\phi\in V,$$
and assign $b_u(t)=0$ on any exceptional null set. Then $b_u(t)\in V^*$ for almost every $t$, $t\mapsto b_u(t)$ is strongly measurable, and its equivalence class is independent of the chosen representative $\widetilde u$. This class belongs to $L^{4/3}(0,T;V^*)$ and satisfies
$$\|b_u(t)\|_{V^*}\le\|\widetilde u(t)\|_{L^4(\Omega)}^2\quad\text{for almost every }t\in(0,T).$$

unforced periodic Leray–Hopf solution with data $(\nu,u_0)$ supplied by Global
periodic weak viscous existence under these hypotheses. Put
$U=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb T_L^d$, and let $\mathcal D_{\rm per}(U)$ be the
space of smooth complex-valued functions on $U$, represented by smooth
$L$-periodic lifts in space, that are compactly supported in time. For tests
supported in a fixed compact interval $K\subset(0,\infty)$, use the seminorms
$$p_{K,m}(\phi)=\max_{j+|\alpha|\le m}\sup_{(t,x)\in K\times\mathbb T_L^d}|\partial_t^j\partial_x^\alpha\phi(t,x)|\qquad(m\in\mathbb N_0);$$
equip $\mathcal D_{\rm per}(U)$ with the locally convex inductive-limit
topology over these fixed-time-support spaces, generated by all seminorms whose
restriction to every fixed-time-support space is continuous. A spacetime distribution means a
continuous complex-linear functional on this test space; all pairings are
bilinear, and derivatives act by transposing the corresponding test derivative
with a minus sign. Then there is a unique mean-zero-in-space
distribution $\pi$ on $(0,\infty)\times\mathbb T_L^d$ such that
$\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)+\nabla\pi=\nu\Delta u$
as a spacetime distribution, normalized by requiring its zero spatial Fourier
coefficient to vanish. Specifically, for $k\in\mathbb Z^d$, its $k$th spatial
Fourier coefficient is the time distribution defined by
$\langle\widehat\pi(k),\psi\rangle=\langle\pi,\psi(t)e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x}\rangle$
for $\psi\in C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\mathbb C)$, with the spacetime
distribution pairing taken using $dt\,L^{-d}dx$ and extended complex-linearly;
normalization means $\widehat\pi(0)=0$. No
function-space or pointwise regularity for $\pi$ is
asserted.
